subject: Life Skills
title: The Zeigarnik Effect
description: A quick win: understand The Zeigarnik Effect.

hook.text: A waitress in a 1920s Berlin cafe remembered every unpaid order perfectly but forgot paid ones instantly.

buildup.text: Psychologist Bluma Zeigarnik studied this. Unfinished tasks stick in your mind far more than completed ones.

discovery.text: Your brain treats an unfinished task like an open browser tab. It keeps running in the background, draining energy.

twist.text: You can hack this. Just starting a task — even for five minutes — partly satisfies the loop and reduces anxiety.

climax.text: Write down your next step for every open task. That small act tricks your brain into releasing some of the tension.

punchline.text: Start it or write down the next step. Close the loop.

quiz.question: What does the Zeigarnik Effect describe?
options: Completed tasks are easier to recall than unfinished ones
Unfinished tasks stay active in memory, causing mental drain
Tasks done quickly are forgotten faster
